title: Cycloidal drive: output flange P2 (PETG-CF)
prompt:
Component analysis: the output flange P2 of an open-source, 3D-printable 15:1 cycloidal gearbox. part.step holds the single solid in millimetres (48 faces, volume 18891 mm^3). faces.json lists every face with its index, type, area, centroid and normal/axis; use the geometry, not a CAD system's own face numbering.

Material: PETG-CF, linear isotropic elastic, E = 3000 MPa, Poisson ratio 0.36.
Analysis: linear static, small displacements, no gravity, no contact.
Supports: all three displacement components are zero on face 17: cylinder, area 471.24 mm^2, centroid (115.525, -7.346, 2.871) mm, radius 30.0 mm, axis (1.0, 0.0, -0.0) through (113.025, 0.0, 20.5) (boss/shaft surface); face 23: cylinder, area 471.24 mm^2, centroid (115.525, 7.346, 38.129) mm, radius 30.0 mm, axis (1.0, 0.0, -0.0) through (113.025, 0.0, 20.5) (boss/shaft surface).
Load: total force (0.000, -69.086, -165.807) N applied as a uniform surface traction (constant force per unit area) over the loaded face(s): face 1 carries (0.000, -11.516, -27.638) N; face 2 carries (0.000, -11.515, -27.637) N; face 3 carries (0.000, -11.518, -27.643) N; face 4 carries (0.000, -11.516, -27.638) N; face 5 carries (0.000, -11.511, -27.626) N; face 6 carries (0.000, -11.511, -27.626) N.
For reference, the source solved this with second-order tetrahedra (Netgen, maximum element size 2 mm).

Outputs:
- max_displacement_mm [mm]: maximum nodal displacement magnitude in the part

Submit results.json containing exactly an outputs object with these numeric keys. Also submit main.py, part.step, mesh.msh, fields.npz, solver.log, refinement.json and environment.json. See candidate README for the artifact contract. Correct numerical answers alone do not establish workflow completion.
